review: Nice rpg in typical fashion.  It has a bittersweet story.  The characters are interesting, and talented fighters.  I recommend playing this game through as the ending is worth it.

The Tale of a Common Man, developed and published by Aldorlea Games, is a deliberately old-school role-playing experience that embraces the spirit of classic 16-bit era JRPGs while layering in modern conveniences and a surprisingly ambitious scope. At its heart is a story rooted in personal tragedy rather than grand prophecy. The protagonist, Jerrat, begins not as a chosen hero or royal heir, but as a simple farmer whose quiet life is destroyed by violence. The loss of his family becomes the catalyst for a journey that expands far beyond revenge, gradually entangling him in political unrest, hidden conspiracies, and threats that stretch across the kingdom. This grounding in ordinary humanity gives the narrative emotional weight, allowing the epic scale of the later chapters to feel earned rather than arbitrary.

The storytelling unfolds at a measured pace, blending personal grief with broader worldbuilding. While the early sections lean heavily into exposition as the setting and its factions are introduced, the narrative gains momentum as party members join Jerrat and their own motivations begin to shape the direction of the adventure. Aldorlea Games is known for dense, content-rich RPGs, and that tradition is evident here. The plot does not rely on flashy cinematic presentation; instead, it builds depth through dialogue, character interactions, and a steady expansion of the world map. Themes of resilience, justice, corruption, and moral compromise surface naturally as Jerrat’s journey evolves from personal vendetta into something more complex and ethically layered.

Visually, the game embraces a vibrant retro aesthetic reminiscent of 1990s console RPGs. Pixel art environments depict towns, forests, caves, castles, and hidden ruins with a colorful palette that emphasizes charm over realism. Character sprites are expressive within the constraints of the style, and enemy designs range from familiar fantasy archetypes to more imaginative creatures. While some indoor locations and town layouts may feel structurally similar, the overall variety of biomes and dungeon themes keeps exploration engaging. The retro presentation is not merely nostalgic window dressing; it reinforces the game’s identity as a love letter to classic RPG design philosophies.

Combat operates within a traditional turn-based system that prioritizes strategy and party composition. Up to five characters can participate in battle simultaneously, chosen from a roster of recruitable allies with different roles and abilities. This larger active party size compared to many classic RPGs allows for layered tactical decisions. Players must balance physical attackers, magic users, healers, and support characters, adjusting their approach depending on enemy formations and boss mechanics. Leveling up grants stat points that can be manually distributed, adding a customization element that rewards planning but also carries consequences. There is no easy respec option, meaning build decisions feel meaningful and permanent.

Difficulty customization is one of the game’s standout features. Players can adjust encounter rates and choose from multiple difficulty levels, making the experience adaptable to both newcomers and veterans. On higher settings, battles demand careful resource management and thoughtful preparation, particularly in longer dungeons where MP conservation and healing items become crucial. On lower settings, the game offers a smoother narrative-focused experience. This flexibility ensures that the adventure can cater to a wide range of playstyles without compromising its core design.

Exploration plays a major role in the game’s structure. The world is filled with optional content, including numerous side quests, hidden rooms, secret characters, and concealed treasures. These elements reward curiosity and thorough map exploration, often providing powerful equipment or narrative insights. Crafting systems such as potion making further incentivize resource gathering, tying exploration into character progression. Players who invest time in uncovering every secret will find the experience significantly richer than those who follow only the main storyline.

The game’s length is substantial, often exceeding thirty hours depending on how thoroughly players engage with optional content. This longevity is both a strength and a potential drawback. For fans of expansive, methodical RPGs, the sheer amount of content provides a satisfying sense of immersion and value. However, the pacing can occasionally feel uneven, with certain stretches leaning into grinding or backtracking. That said, the adjustable encounter rate helps mitigate potential fatigue, allowing players to streamline travel when necessary.

Musically, the soundtrack complements the retro aesthetic with melodic, fantasy-inspired tracks that enhance towns, battles, and dramatic story moments. While not bombastic, the music reinforces the emotional tone of each region and maintains consistency throughout the lengthy campaign. Sound effects and battle cues are functional and nostalgic, contributing to the overall sense of playing a modernized classic rather than a contemporary cinematic RPG.

Ultimately, The Tale of a Common Man succeeds by committing wholeheartedly to its identity. It does not attempt to reinvent the genre, nor does it chase modern AAA trends. Instead, it focuses on delivering a heartfelt, content-rich, turn-based RPG experience grounded in character growth and traditional mechanics. Its emotional core, expansive world, strategic combat system, and wealth of optional content make it particularly appealing to players who appreciate classic design sensibilities. For those who long for the era of pixelated adventures filled with side quests, party management, and slow-burn storytelling, this title offers a substantial and earnest journey that rewards patience, strategy, and dedication.

Rating: 8/10

I've played a lot of smaller scale indie/RPG maker games, some of them are bad or totally generic but this one stands out as having had a particular amount of love put into it. The story is a relatively standard arc about you Jerrat the farmer having your farm destroyed and family killed, and setting off on a journey to bring the people responsible to justice. You'll meet many other party members along the way that join your quest for various reasons, and I have to say I took a liking to most of them. I appreciated the game gives you a lot of customization options in terms of forming your party with the members you want and being able to allocate bonus points upon leveling up to give you a further degree of control over your statistical spread. 

The game also features a pretty varied amount of side quests, some more compelling than others but none that stick out as just padding, some of it was quite fun! I'm glad the game also rewards you for exploring with items and stat boosting items littered on the landscape and in one of the 30 secret rooms in the game. I wouldn't say it's that grind heavy but I think if you want to enjoy all the side content you may have to put in some time raising your party a few levels, as some of the optional bosses and even the main bosses at the end of the game are quite tough and will really challenge you, but not in a way that seems unfair. The combat is varied and complex enough (turn based) to be able to form different strategies depending on the foes you're facing.

You can also find equipment and accessories in various shops and in places around the game world, but it seemed that ultimately your stat development is more important which I think is a good focus. The game wasn't overly long either, and I got 100% in about 15 hours and a pretty satisfying conclusion at the end. If you're someone who likes JRPGs in general and are looking for something new to try out I definitely recommend giving this a shot, the art style was unique enough and I enjoyed my experience with this game. If you're on the fence pick it up on sale, but I'd still recommend this at $10.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

The Tale of a Common Man очередная jRPG, собранная на RPG Maker. Кто сталкивался с данным движком прекрасно понимает, что его ожидает, вплоть до способностей существ, накладываемых ими эффектов и ролевой моделью. Единственный плюс игры - неплохой сюжет, правда в нём практически нет интересных поворотов, но в целом истории мести всегда получаются как минимум поучительными. У обычного фермера убивают жену и ребёнка, после чего он отправляется на поиски ублюдков по пути решаю проблемы спутников и жителей местных городов. В нашем приключении нам могут помочь 7 компаньонов, среди которых особняком выделяется разумный бобёр. Правда их присоединение выходят сумбурными, из разряда я тоже не понимаю что делаю в жизни, но с тобой мне будет веселее. Теперь о минусах, в игре практически нет запоминающихся сражений, даже финальный босс оказывается группой из 5 обычных людей плюс призванная горилла. Вторая проблема абсолютная линейность в выполнении основного квеста, при этом ряд побочных выглядят куда интереснее, чем заглавная история. При этом одно из заданий имеет интересное продолжение. Третья проблема - ужасный дисбаланс, маги настолько имбовы, что за пару заклинаний выкашивают всех монстров, главное найти к какой стихии они уязвимы.  В итоге, не играя в The Tale of a Common Man вы в принципе ничего не пропустите, ну а если всё таки взяли тоже не беда, 12 неплохих часов обеспечены. Середняк, 6.0 из 10.

A most unlikely set of adventures each with their own priorities brought together. It worked for me. However, it certainly made me think about the out-come. The developers I feel got it right.

For me I would have liked to have seen more of the 3D adventures in game rather than waiting till the end. That said, an excellent idea to give you a run down on how each of your party faired in and out of battle... Nice... No spoilers. If you enjoy RPG's I would certainly recommend giving it a try.

Enjoyed it.  I was surprised by how good a game it was to be honest.  I really enjoyed the dialogue between the characters and the fact that you could see what characters were thinking at given points was a great way to give them more life.  Combat is ok...it gets deeper as the the game progresses.  Satisfying end to the story.  The only qualm I have is the respawning enemies when you leave a map and come back to it.  Fighting the same types of monsters over and over on certain tilesets can become repetitive.  That being said it was money well spent.  Thanks for the fun game!

Another Aldorlea game in the bag so time for a review!   This game is harder to quantify than those before it since for example Dreamscape has a better battle system in my opinion, but this game has a far better story.  Although again a simple one.  The emotion put into the performance both sad and happy at times is what made this game.

On the other hand this game has the flaw of you really need the guide for it the secret rooms are sometimes a little too well hidden.  But this does not detract from how fufilling this game is.  And the pairings actually make sense.  

However this game at normal and probably hard difficulty has a rather odd problem.  Virtually every character is a 'physical' character in which the MAT stat is virtually worthless. And the one 'mage' you do have learns moves too slow and aren't strong enough to really do much for what she really needs to do.  When I got the final party member I perma benched her, since you can do a pretty awesome combo if you do galvanize+enthuse friends for 33% crits on top of increased attack, and add in dropping enemies defenses?  Even better!

Though there are a few skills in the game that are bugged for example Quinacrodrone instead of reducing an enemies' defense it decreases your own defense.   And pump up the action only adds counter onto one ally not all.

But still another gem of a game by Aldorlea.

Здравствуй игрок. Ты остановился на выборе этой игры, но ты не уверен? Бери ее смело, эта игра заставила меня пустить скупую мужскую слезу в конце, я думаю она не оставит никого равнодушным, прошел ее на легендарной сложности, то еще удовольствие: получил реальный челледж, сопартийцы сбалансированы, обдумываешь на ход вперед, иногда бывают моменты когда становится легко, но ровно до того момента пока не перешагнешь на следующую часть архипелага.
Итак к плюсам: 
1) сюжет вдаваться в подробности не буду нужно самому читать, чтобы было интересно
2) поиск секреток - секретные комнатки это наше все=)
3) механика игры - трудно добываемый шмот, крафт зелий, использование аксессуаров в различных ситуациях
4) карточки - мне выпала металлическая карточка Джеррада которая стоит в разы больше, чем сама игра купленная на распродаже=)
Итак к минусам:
1) Для кого то это может быть минусом, но не для меня - это игра RPG Maker и этим все сказано
2) В основном это линейность, но тут наши действия обосновываются персонажами, так что плюс / минус.
3) Необходим средний уровень Инглиша, без него боюсь смысла брать ее нету.
Ps: Игра очень хорошо сделана, хорошо сбалансирована, отличный сюжет, местами великолепный саунд трек, хотелось бы конечно, чтобы можно было немного больше исследовать мир, но и так в принципе отлично.
Берите однозначно, если не пугает RPG Maker  и владеете английским языком на среднем уровне.
Muy recomendado si sois de la vieja escuela,me recordo mis primeros tiempos jugando juegos de rol,la trama es bastante buena y la forma de jugar sencilla.

Old school JRPG with turn based fighting and points to spend when you level up. That's the itch I look to scratch, and so rarely does a game do it so well. I loved almost everything about this game. Almost. I didn't like being forced down a path, and restricted from certain areas. Not being allowed to back track and explore kind of irritated me, but it really became a problem when I couldn't get passed a certain part in the story because I didn't put any DEF onto a certain character, causing him to get 1 shot and not allowing me to leave the city. So had to load a previous save to grind some levels for him. Still worth the money, I hope to find more games like this.

Generic grinding combat paired with a story that keeps telling you to go grind. Remarkably poor writing on a technical level combined with absolutely no sense of subtlety, as Jerrat tells the player that he loves his family and will be sad now that they're dead and swears revenge because he is angry and is bad at fighting because he is a common man, as the story then poorly meshes with the gameplay as Jerrat proceeds to have trouble beating up rats despite regularly going to the forest to pick mushrooms. Add in the clumsy pairing of original art and stock RPGMaker assets and you have an all around mediocre game that I see no reason to bother sitting through any longer.

Recently played the game and finished it on normal mode.

I liked the following:
1) Interesting and fun conversations between each characters.
2) Character's thoughts are conveyed throughout the game, which makes the content and gameplay enjoyable.
3) Interesting system where you cannot just barge into civilian's houses and loot (like your average classic RPGs ;D)
4) The stroy was quite short in my perspective, but the storyline do just go straight to the point.

Suggestions for the game:
(a) The world map appears to be "locked-route" and it would be better-off if players are given the option to be able to re-visit without being barred from the main story.
(b) The side quest may be better if they are not time-event bound.
(c) The varieties of enemies can be improved, exepcially for bosses.
(d) There should be options for post-end game plays where you are able to attend to side quests or finding secret rooms in my opinion.
(e) If only other characters may also be optional to join the party while on the quest...

Overall it is quite a nice game with its own pros and cons. I would recommend it to friends who are interested in RPGMaker type of games.

This game starts with tragedy. A roving army has lost some of its food supplies, so they pillage a local farm for supplies... and kill a woman and baby. Unfortunately for them they missed their husband/father, who was working in the fields... and now he's out for blood.

Thus a common farmer is thrust into a epic adventure of revenge and saving the world (because waht else do you need?). Can he complete this task without losing the man who his wife loved?

Looks fun.

C'est un jeu de rôles de RPG Maker, mais il est conçu pour couvrir la formule JRPG d'une manière très différente ... une façon qui regarde le monde des yeux d'un homme commun qui cherche une vengeance.
 
Les joueurs prendront le rôle de fermier commun appelé Jerrat qui cherche la vengeance après que sa femme et son fils sont brutalement assassinés.

L'aventure voit Jerrat accompagné d'autres guerriers et aventuriers en cours de route, tentant de se venger tout en jouant un complot beaucoup plus compliqué qui affectera le destin de la nation. Jerrat doit également se battre contre ses propres démons, dans l'espoir de ne pas se laisser consommer par la haine qui le conduit à sa quête et de maintenir les principes fondamentaux qui ont conduit à sa femme à l'amoureux de lui dès le début.

Le conte d'un homme commun est un jeu de réflexion inspirée de 16 bits avec un combat tourné, sept personnages pouvant rejoindre le parti, cinq personnages actifs pendant le combat, 30 salles secrètes et 30 heures de jeu

"Les graphismes du jeu m'ont plu. Bien sûr, ce n'est pas le plus remarquable, mais tout semble soigné et attrayant. Tous les milieux et les personnages sont dessinés avec amour.

"Les combats ici sont les mêmes que dans n'importe quel JRPG. Leur complexité dépend du niveau de difficulté que vous choisissez au début du jeu. "

C'est un jeu de rpg-maker, donc si cela vous dérange, ce n'est peut-être pas votre tasse de thé. Si toutefois, vous aimez jouer à un jeu difficile à la fois drôle et intelligent, alors vous l'apprécierez. J'ai fait. Le temps de jeu était d'environ 10 à 12 heures. Pas mal pour un jeu peu coûteux! "...

I enjoyed this game.  I like that we get to see a lot of the inner thoughts of the characters, and watch their personal progression.  Combat was decent, good pixel art, though the outfits were silly nonsense.  Good ending.

I like that there was a lot of world I didn't get to visit, as the characters had good reason to not just wander half a continent away -- they were on a deadline.  Yet those areas existed anyway, to give the world life.  There's more towns and cities than you can visit.  Also there's a lot of doorways you can't enter, because of course homeowners and shopkeepers don't want you rummaging through their stuff.  My primary compulsion as an RPG player is to loot everything, but we're playing as characters who generally don't do that.  Nice touch.  :D

Big complaint was controls.  Controller didn't work, F12 surprisingly restarts the game instead of taking a screenshot (so I had to play the final battle again to see the rest of the ending -- oops!), and keys were not remappable.  It wasn't crippling, but it was very inconvenient.

This game was well designed, it never felt like I was over-powered, and I was always having to think about combat even up to the end of the game. I really like the writing also - it was clever and engaging. The party banter was quite funny in spots (you can listen in on their thoughts sometimes). It's an rpg-maker game, so if that bothers you, this may not be your cup of tea. If however, you like playing a challenging game that is both funny and clever, then you will enjoy it. I did. Game time was about 10-12 hours. Not bad for an inexpensive game! Have fun!
